question: In which year was the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development adopted by the United Nations Member States?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2015**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development was adopted by all United Nations Member States on **25 September 2015**.
 
• It provides a shared blueprint for peace and prosperity for people and the planet, now and into the future.
 
• This agenda includes **17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, which are an urgent call to action for all countries.
 
• The SDGs aim to address global challenges, including poverty, inequality, climate change, environmental degradation, peace, and justice.
 
• Implementation of the agenda is a collective responsibility, emphasizing partnerships between governments, businesses, civil society, and individuals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):**

 
 
• The SDGs consist of 17 goals and 169 targets, addressing issues such as poverty eradication, quality education, gender equality, and climate action.
 
• They replace the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), which were operational from 2000 to 2015.
 
 
 
• **Key Principles of the 2030 Agenda:**
 
 
• The agenda emphasizes universality, integration, and leaving no one behind.
 
• It aims to balance the three dimensions of sustainable development: economic, social, and environmental.
 
 
 
• **Partnerships for the Goals:**
 
 
• SDG 17 focuses on strengthening partnerships globally to achieve the goals.
 
• It includes commitments to financial, technological, and capacity-building support for developing nations.
 
 
 
• **Monitoring and Reporting:**
 
 
• Each country is encouraged to conduct regular reviews of progress toward the SDGs, known as Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs).
 
• The United Nations High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) serves as the central platform for reviewing the agenda's implementation.
